chapter: Hollywood and the break with Thornhill
title: Victor session of 1 March 1938 and the change of label
summary: Hughes lists the titles; she guesses the short Vocalion contract lapsed.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: So we've been discussing the recording session of February 4, 1938. Four songs on it -- "It's Wonderful", "Dark Eyes", "A Brown Bird Sings" and "You Went To My Head."
Yes.
The next recording session
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
you made was the 1st of March in the same year.
Yes.
For Victor this time.
Yes.
Maybe you have some thought about the change of labels that have the --
I really don't --
Can I just give the titles before we --
Yes.
The titles were, 'Moments Like This', 'Please Be Kind', 'It Was A Lover And His Lass,' lyrics by William Shakespeare -- and another version of 'Ochi Chornia' or ('Dark Eyes').
I beleived it was called in England actually 'Dark Eyes'.
Yes.
Sorry, I interrupted.
It's all right.
I don't know -- I guessed that the contract that I had with Vocalion was just limited to a certain number of sides anyway.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Because I was new, there's a possibility that it was just a trial balloon, so to speak. And out of the bunch of tunes -- you know what I mean -- "Lock Lomond" was very hard to top.
So, maybe they just didn't sell as well as --
Well I think what happened was, I only had that short-time contract. And Claude had arranged for a contract with Victor.
So he selected these things -- "A Lover and His Lass" -- and I don't know whether you noticed "Lover and His Lass" we used Dave Barbour as a guitarist on the record.
But there was no part for guitar. And so Claude handed him in the bird whistle (and said), "If you listen to Lover and His Lass, you'll hear that bird whistle."
I don't know how many people played the record out to the last groove, but at the end, there is a door slammed.
